Subject: BYOK waterfall cutover: rotation drill, cross-connect failover & emergency rollback protocol

Paul / Acme secops team —

Thanks again for agreeing to the phased BYOK cutover drill next week. Attached is the initial "waterfall" plan (byok-waterfall-plan-v1.pdf) and the evidence checklist we will capture during the window (evidence-checklist.xlsx). High level asks and context: 

- Goal: practice a full production-analog cutover where customer-managed keys (BYOK) are moved to the target HSM cluster, rotated, and exercised end-to-end with cross-connect failover.
- Window: Tue 2026-05-25 02:00–06:00 UTC (proposed). We'll run in staging first (same network topology), then repeat in the production maintenance window if staging is green.
- Key mechanics summary (short): rewrap current tenant KEKs on source HSM, activate temporary proxy key on staging HSM pair, perform split-commit rotation, validate token-level decrypts, then rotate primary tenant KEK out-of-band and publish new wrapping keys.
- Emergency rollback ("netlock"): network-level lockdown + immediate HSM snapshot restore path if we detect >10% failure in token decrypts after step 3. Detailed rollback steps included in the plan.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Can you confirm the fiber cross-connect failover window (your side) between us-east-1a and your on-prem CPE? We need BGP holdtime tolerances.
2) Firmware baseline: do you require us to run with HSM firmware 4.8.x or is 4.9.x acceptable for the staging exercise?
3) Operator separation: do you want a pre-approved set of operator principals from your SRE team for the drill, or should we use the standard operator cohort listed in the plan?

Immediate next steps if this window works: we will run a preflight checklist (NTP, CRL/OCSP, PKCS#11 endpoint sanity) 48h prior and gather attestation artifacts into the evidence pack. Please reply with the answers above and any additional constraints.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.io
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: BYOK waterfall cutover: rotation drill, cross-connect failover & emergency rollback protocol

Jordan —

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifying points from our end before we sign off on the window: 

- Cross-connect: We can flex the BGP holdtime down to 30s during the window, but will need a short pre-notice to schedule the fibre ops team.
- Firmware: Our HSM fleet is currently on 4.8.7 across the on-prem primary; we prefer not to upgrade to 4.9.x for the drill. Confirm Redwood runtime supports 4.8.7 with the rewrap path.
- K-of-N split: We need to confirm the threshold for the tenant KEK split (you proposed 2-of-3 in the doc). Can we make that configurable in the drill so we can test 3-of-5 as well?
- NTP / time sync: we require NTP tested and signed with our internal NTP pool prior to any signature operations — please include that in the preflight.

I am also looping in our partner CloudBridge (integration@cloudbridge.io) — they maintain the HSM bridge we use for TLS termination to your runtime. They will share an attestation PDF for the firmware compatibility.

Paul Evans
Director, Platform Security | AcmeCorp
paul.evans@acmecorp.com

Subject: Re: BYOK waterfall cutover: rotation drill, cross-connect failover & emergency rollback protocol

Paul — thanks, good notes. Responding inline and adding a few operational details so we have them in thread: 

- Cross-connect: BGP holdtime 30s is fine. We'll add a brief pre-notice to your fiber ops (T-72h). We'll also instrument a BFD probe on the test cross-connect for aggressive detection during the drill.

- Firmware: Redwood runtime is validated on HSM 4.8.7; the rewrap path uses standard PKCS#11 sessions and will not call any 4.9-only APIs. We will include the CloudBridge attestation in the evidence pack.

- Split threshold: the drill plan is parameterized — we can run a 2-of-3 first pass, then a 3-of-5 pass if you want. Expected timing delta: 2-of-3 completes ~6–8 minutes faster due to fewer coordination steps; 3-of-5 is good to validate quorum behavior and operator latencies.

- NTP: agreed — NTP signed responses will be validated during preflight. We'll perform signed NTP verification and include the signed timestamp proof in the evidence bundle.

Emergency rollback (netlock) — clarified: 
1) Detection: monitor token-level decrypt success rate and API error spike.
2) Lock: temporarily toggle ACLs on the tenant route to prevent new write operations (we'll maintain read-only traffic during assessment).
3) Restore: if rollback criteria hit (>=10% token decrypt failures for 5 minutes), we will invoke the HSM snapshot restore on the staging HSM pair, rewrap the KEK set to the previous wrapping key, and publish a rollback announcement.

Operational notes: PKCS#11 endpoints will be reachable at pkcs11.acme.internal:5696 (staging) and require mutual TLS. We will hand over a short script set to your SREs to run the verify and rewrap steps.

Triage owner on our side will be David Kim (copied). Kimberly will manage the evidence pack collation. Tessa — can we schedule a staging run Friday 2026-05-21 22:00 UTC to rehearse?
